bibliographic.title: Leveraging large language models in patient-reported outcome measure development: practical opportunities, cautions, and a human-in-the-loop roadmap
bibliographic.citation_apa: Mara, C., & Rybak, T. (2026). Leveraging large language models in patient-reported outcome measure development: Practical opportunities, cautions, and a human-in-the-loop roadmap. Journal of Patient-Reported Outcomes, 10, 93. https://doi.org/10.1186/s41687-026-01112-2

methodology.method_family: editorial commentary with illustrative project examples
methodology.sample_description: Illustrative examples from the Eating Behavior Measurement (EBM) pediatric PRO development project; draws on emerging literature from PRO science, survey methodology, and psychological measurement
methodology.technology_context: LLMs as structured drafting and analytic tools for qualitative phases of patient-reported outcome measure development, not deployed conversational systems

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article addresses human-in-the-loop governance, oversight, transparency, and risk mitigation for LLM use in a regulated healthcare context, but focuses on PRO measure qualitative development workflows rather than conversational AI systems, chatbots, agents, or operational governance of deployed conversational LLM applications.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python triage flagged central_candidate despite conversational_ai score 0/3; adjudication needed on whether non-conversational human-in-the-loop LLM governance qualifies as in-scope supporting evidence.

appraisal.notes: Peer-reviewed editorial commentary appropriately proposes a practical roadmap and discusses risks, but is not an empirical or systematic study; evidence base is illustrative and literature-informed rather than systematically sampled.

cerqual.explanation: The human-in-the-loop roadmap is internally coherent and transparent about LLM limits, but as a commentary it offers moderate methodological adequacy and only partial relevance to conversational governance because the LLM use cases are bounded drafting and analytic workflows in PRO development.

coding.theme: Human-in-the-loop governance for bounded LLM assistance in regulated healthcare measurement workflows
coding.subtheme: PRO qualitative development rather than conversational system deployment

synthesis.main_claim: LLMs can support systematic and scalable qualitative PRO development workflows when used as bounded drafting and analytic tools under rigorous human oversight, but they do not replace qualitative inquiry, expert judgment, or empirical psychometric validation.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes a practical human-in-the-loop roadmap with bounded use cases and explicit cautions about confirmation bias, semantic circularity, transparency, reproducibility, and construct drift in healthcare PRO development.
synthesis.limitations: Commentary format with illustrative EBM project examples; does not evaluate deployed conversational LLM systems or provide empirical validation of the proposed roadmap.
synthesis.use_in_review: Include as supporting evidence for human-in-the-loop oversight, transparency, and risk-mitigation patterns in regulated healthcare LLM workflows; exclude from central conversational-governance evidence because the application domain is PRO measure development rather than conversational AI.
